concept: Reference self-flip floor from cache_prompt and batch-size nondeterminism
summary: A llama.cpp user running 8 server slots with temperature 0, a fixed seed and cache_prompt false got 5 to 8 distinct completions from the same prompt on an H100, reproduced on an M1 MacBook Pro and an A100, and always one completion with one slot but still small logit variations.

facts.text: A llama.cpp user running 8 server slots with temperature 0, a fixed seed and cache_prompt false got 5 to 8 distinct completions from the same prompt on an H100, reproduced on an M1 MacBook Pro and an A100, and always one completion with one slot but still small logit variations.

A llama.cpp maintainer's answer: bit-identical floating point output needs the exact same operations in the same order, and multiple slots are faster precisely because they do not run that way; multi-slot output stayed not fully deterministic on master, and a per-slot RNG fix (PR 6835) was needed because slots first shared one RNG state.
The issue was closed by the stale bot after 14 days with no root-cause fix.

vLLM documents "batch invariance" as an opt-in beta (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1) that makes output independent of batch size and request order, supported on NVIDIA GPUs of compute capability 8.0 or higher and Intel XPUs with Triton; Apple GPUs are not listed.
No llama.cpp or MLX switch with the vLLM guarantee was found, so on a Mac the floor has to be measured, not configured away.

KLD analogue: llama-perplexity derives n_seq from n_batch / n_ctx and runs sequences together, so the reference pass and each candidate pass use batch shapes set by -b and -c; the candidate pass must reuse the reference's -c, and equal -b is the only way to keep batch composition equal.

A direct floor measurement: run the reference file's own model through the --kl-divergence pass with a different -b and read mean KLD and Same-top p; any nonzero KLD or Same-top p under 100% is the batch-shape floor.
2024-05: issue 7052 reports the multi-slot effect. 2025-2026: vLLM adds batch invariance (docs read 2026-10-04).
Single-slot variation in logits does not necessarily change argmax, but a near-tie position can flip, so the floor concentrates on low-margin positions, the same positions a quant flips.
The issue's hardware was CUDA plus one M1 report; Metal reduction order differs, so the size of the floor on Apple GPUs is unknown.

"Greedy plus cache_prompt false is deterministic enough" (implied by the harness recipe in the covering file) versus the 7052 evidence of 5 to 8 distinct outputs across slots. The issue used many slots; one slot gave one completion.
Self-flip rate of a Metal llama-server with one slot, cache_prompt on versus off, and across -ub values, on a 1,000-position token stream.
Whether MLX has a batch-size-dependent reduction order that makes mlx_lm.server self-flip.
Issue 7052 reports 5 to 8 unique completions from 8 slots at temperature 0 with cache_prompt false, and one completion with a single slot.
The same issue reports the effect on an M1 MacBook Pro as well as an H100 and an A100.
The llama.cpp maintainer attributes the multi-slot variation to differing floating-point operation order across slots.
vLLM batch invariance is beta, opt-in, and listed for NVIDIA compute capability 8.0 or higher and Intel XPU only.
llama-perplexity sets n_seq from n_batch divided by n_ctx, so batch settings shape how sequences are grouped in both reference and candidate passes.
No measurement of a Metal llama-server or mlx_lm.server self-flip floor was found.
